annotations.text: Forecasts: one roof for what is coming

The brief

Everything the app says about what has not happened yet lives in three places: What's coming under Money, What to buy under Buy, The day under Insight. Three doors, one question — what is coming — asked at three horizons.

They become one screen under Insight, called Forecasts, with a lens for each horizon: Today (hours), Stock (days), Cash (the next 30 days).

Nothing in the engine changes. cashAhead, purchasePlan and renderDay keep their names and every law they own; each draws into a lens instead of a section of its own.

The roof is the point, not the menu

One strip on every lens, and it is the reason these are one screen rather than three neighbours:

Safe to spend is what the buying plan budgets from. The plan is what the shelf needs before it runs out. What ran out today is on the shelf list. Today's takings are where next month's cash comes from.

Each tile is another lens's headline. Switching never loses the figure you switched away from — and the dependency the code has always had (renderPurchasePlanPanel reads cashAhead().safeToSpend) is finally visible on the screen.

What "forecast" is allowed to mean here

What to buy's own help text says "nothing here is a forecast — every figure comes from an invoice or the Price Registry". That law holds under this roof.

A run-out day is the shelf divided by a 30-day rate. The cash line is the drawer minus bills somebody dated. A typical Tuesday is the middle of the last five. Every figure is derived, never invented — and each tile says what it is derived from.

The word on the door is the owner's word for these, and the sub-line under it is where the app keeps its honesty.

Cash opens first

It is the figure the other two lenses depend on, and the question the owner asks before any purchase: can I commit money today, and when does that stop being true?

The runway is .design/ahead's, unchanged: a step line, a dashed ghost for promises, the low point named where it happens. The undated bills moved from a third panel below the fold into the rail, beside the act that puts them on the line.

No accent on a healthy day. Naming a day is a row-level act; when the line goes under, the accent is "Chase these three", in the rail, as .design/ahead drew it.

Stock keeps its shape

On the way first (a buyer who cannot see it buys it twice), then the plan, then what is over the budget. The rail's arithmetic reads straight off the Cash lens: the same two figures, the same walk.

The header carries the app's two fields, Cover and Budget, because the plan turns on them. Redo the plan moved into the plan's own head to keep the header on one line beside the lens.

The accent is the basket bar, pinned at the foot, and only once something is ticked. Nothing is sent from here.

The day, honestly

The day is a record. Its own comment says so: "as at that day, never as at now". Nothing on it predicts.

What IS ahead on it: what a typical Tuesday ends at (the same median the verdict uses — an expectation, not a verdict), what stands between today and being closed, and the Manager's pace on the week's target ("at this rate the week ends at"), which the dashboard already derives without a meeting.

So the Today lens leads with those and keeps the record — the stepper walks back to a closed day in the same shape, and Print the day stays.

If you would rather The day stayed a door of its own under Insight, Forecasts is two lenses and loses nothing else.

Not enough is an answer

A strip reading 0, 0, 0, 0 makes a new shop look like a broken app. Each tile says what it is waiting for instead: a cash book opened today, 14 days of sales to read a rate from, an earlier Tuesday.

No line is drawn from a figure nobody recorded. The one accent is the act that starts it.

What the rail loses, and what search keeps

Buy loses What to buy, Money loses What's coming, Insight loses The day and gains Forecasts. No seventh group, so the six-wrapper count both nav tests pin stays true.

Every old name and keyword is donated to the Forecasts row — "what to buy", "runs out", "cash forecast", "safe to spend", "yesterday" — so the word already in the owner's head still lands. "stock" is NOT taken: it belongs to Inventory, as the rail's own comments insist.

resolveTab gains three aliases — ahead, buying, day — each setting the lens and returning 'forecasts', the way stock-movements already lands on Inventory. The Manager's doors, the dashboard's "See what falls due", and the assistant's tab list keep working.

The tests this turns into decisions

1. admin-nav's "visible >= 26" counts destinations on the rail at rest; folding three rows into one makes it 24. The assertion's point (nothing behind a menu) still holds — the number does not.

2. design-system.test.js pins CONVERTED specs for day, ahead and buying by section id; purchase-plan.test.js pins id="tab-buying", data-tab="buying" and the dispatch line verbatim. When the three sections become one, each of those is re-argued, not patched.

3. cash-ahead.test.js asserts the strip opens on Safe to spend — the roof keeps it first.

Nothing about the engines' own tests moves.

Not decided for you

1. Whether The day belongs here at all (see the red note). The artboards assume yes because you asked; the alternative costs nothing.

2. What the lens counts mean. Drawn as the things wanting a decision: 1 closing check, 7 lines to buy, 19 bills with no day. They could as easily be the window's payments (6) or nothing.

3. Which lens Forecasts opens on. Cash, here, because the other two budget from it. Today is the other defensible answer.

4. The rail row carries no badge. What to buy, What's coming and The day never had one, and a number on a door that means three different things means nothing.

The phone is its own design

The lens is full width under the name, 44px tall. The roof folds to 2×2 with short figures — 2.11m, not 2,110,000 — because four eight-digit figures in 358px is a strip nobody can read.

Cash keeps the chart, stripped: no low-point label, no legend. The roof already said the figures; the small chart adds the shape.

Stock is a card a line, the tick a full-width labelled button, and the basket docked in the thumb as the one accent — the pattern Debtors, Creditors and Follow-ups already ship.
